values: Before calling or emailing a lead, search the sheet first. If the project is not already there, add it and set Claimed By to MAX or OWNER before making contact. If it is already claimed, the other person should not contact it.
1. Search Permit / Project # AND Project Address. Red permit/address cells mean a duplicate. Check spelling, unit numbers and nearby addresses too.
2. One row per project. Use a stable manual Lead ID such as VV-0001. Use the full permit number and consistent address including unit and city.
3. Claim before contact. MAX is blue, OWNER purple, UNCLAIMED or blank amber. Confirm the other person has not claimed it at the same time.
4. After contact, update Stage, Last Contact Date, Method, Result, Next Action and Follow-up Date. Keep a short dated history in Notes.
5. Open Follow-ups every morning. It sorts overdue and upcoming dates first and excludes WON, LOST and DO NOT CONTACT. Edit records in Leads.
6. Use Stage for current position. Never contact DO NOT CONTACT. WON is green. LOST and DO NOT CONTACT are muted red. HIGH priority is orange.
7. Relevant VV Scope is a comma-separated field. Copy scope names from Lists. Fit Score is optional manual 1–5, with 5 the strongest fit.
8. Enter amounts as numbers in CAD. Permit Value is the permit total, not the VV opportunity. Quote Value is one current VV quote amount, not summed revisions. Leave unknown amounts blank.

9. Optional conversion history: record First Interested Date, First Quote Requested Date and First Quote Sent Date once when each event first occurs. Retain them after WON or LOST. These columns are grouped at the far right.

10. Counts use current stage. Contacted therefore means currently CONTACTED. Conversion rates use recorded dates, including closed leads. Blank denominator = blank rate. Quote includes requested or sent.
11. Examples contains three fictional rows only. Do not contact them. Leads starts empty. Dashboard and Follow-ups read only Leads.
12. Lists contains editable dropdown choices and scope labels. Keep entries contiguous below each header. All dates use YYYY-MM-DD.
13. Prepared for 500 leads. Extend table, validations and formulas if you exceed row 501. Claiming is a coordination rule, not a technical lock.
14. Share this file with the owner as Editor through Google Sheets Share. Use the exact Google account. Both people must use this same sheet.
